name: TCP throughput ceiling
blurb: A fast link is not a fast transfer. One connection is capped by its window and by packet loss, and on a long path the cap is far below what was paid for.

inputs.label: Round-trip time
inputs.description: Milliseconds there and back. London to Sydney is about 250.

inputs.label: Packet loss
inputs.description: Percent. A tenth of a percent is unremarkable on a long path and costs more than people expect.

inputs.label: Receive window
inputs.description: Kilobytes the receiver will accept unacknowledged. 64 is the largest TCP could express before window scaling.

inputs.label: Segment size
inputs.description: Payload bytes per packet. 1460 on Ethernet; 9000-byte jumbo frames give about 8960.

inputs.label: Chart
inputs.description: Which variable the curve moves. Against loss the two ceilings cross; against distance they fall together and never cross.

links.label: Mathis et al., the sqrt(p) result
